🧭 Explore the Learning Areas

Year 2 Science
🧠

2.0 Human

Human reproduction and the nervous system.

Learning standards
  • 2.1.1 Describe the functions of male and female reproductive organs.
  • 2.1.2 Explain human fertilisation until the baby is born.
  • 2.1.3 Give reasons for the importance of reproduction.
  • 2.2.1 Identify the central and peripheral nervous systems.
  • 2.2.2–2.2.5 Describe functions, predict effects of impairment and suggest ways to care for the nervous system.
  • 2.1.4 and 2.2.6 Communicate observations creatively using writing, speech, sketches or ICT.

Activities: Human Reproduction Poster, Nervous System Signalling Activity, Nervous System Mini Showcase.

🔬

3.0 Microorganism

Types, life processes, growth and effects of microorganisms.

Learning standards
  • 3.1.1 Explain types of microorganisms with examples.
  • 3.1.2 Generalise the meaning of microorganisms.
  • 3.1.3 Investigate life processes of microorganisms.
  • 3.1.4 Experiment to determine factors affecting microorganism growth.
  • 3.1.5 Describe effects of microorganisms in daily life.
  • 3.1.6 Communicate observations creatively through writing, speech, sketches or ICT.

Activities listed in the sheet: Microorganism Detective, Life Processes of Microorganisms, Experiment Suitable Temperature, Mold Terrarium.

🐝

4.0 Interaction Among Living Things

Competition and symbiosis among animals and plants.

Learning standards
  • 4.1.1 Describe types of interaction among living things.
  • 4.1.2 Explain competition among animals within and between species.
  • 4.1.3 Explain mutualism, commensalism and parasitism among animals with examples.
  • 4.1.4 Communicate observations about animal interactions creatively.
  • 4.2.1 Investigate factors of competition among plants.
  • 4.2.2 Explain types of symbiosis among plants.
  • 4.2.3 Communicate observations about plant interactions creatively.

Activities: Interaction Detective, Symbiosis Challenge, Plant Competition Investigation, Symbiosis Gallery Walk.

🌿

5.0 Preservation and Conservation

Protecting animals, plants and the balance of nature.

Learning standards
  • 5.1.1 State the meaning of preservation and conservation.
  • 5.1.2 Generate ideas for preserving and conserving animals and plants.
  • 5.1.3 Explain examples of extinct animals.
  • 5.1.4 Explain examples of threatened animals and plants.
  • 5.1.5 Describe factors that cause extinction threats.
  • 5.1.6 Generate ideas on the effects of preservation and conservation.
  • 5.1.7 Communicate observations creatively and explain one's role in sustainability.

Activity: Threat of Extinction to Animals and Plants Visual Exhibition.

📝 Notes for Implementation

Teacher planning support

1. Plan from the standards

Choose the Learning Standard first, then plan a clear learning objective, activity and evidence that matches it. Use the Performance Standard descriptors in the supplied sheet to guide assessment.

2. Teach through inquiry

Use observe–ask–predict–investigate–record–explain routines. Let pupils discuss evidence, use labelled drawings or tables, and share conclusions in English at an age-appropriate level.

3. Assess during learning

Collect evidence through questioning, observation checklists, pupils’ work, oral explanations and short exit tickets. Give feedback and reteach where misconceptions appear.

4. Safety and sensitivity

For microorganism activities, do not culture unknown samples or open mould containers; use teacher-prepared visuals or sealed demonstrations. Teach human reproduction respectfully, scientifically and in line with school guidance.

Performance Standard: evidence guide

Use the specific Performance Standard for each Learning Standard in the source sheet. This guide helps plan evidence; it does not replace the official descriptors.

PL 1 · Identify / State
Label, point out, name or state with support as appropriate.
PL 2 · Describe
Give relevant details using a sentence, drawing or table.
PL 3 · Explain / Apply
Explain a relationship or apply learning to a given situation.
PL 4–6 · Extend / Communicate
Where the source standard provides these levels, analyse, justify, evaluate or communicate findings creatively.

📘 Curriculum Overview

Standards-led planning

Use the Learning Area, Content Standard, Learning Standard, Activities and Performance Standard columns in the embedded sheet to plan lessons and connect activities to assessment.

Learning areas shown in the provided reference begin with 2.0 Human, followed by 3.0 Microorganism, 4.0 Interaction Among Living Things and 5.0 Preservation and Conservation.

🎨 Teaching Ideas

🪧 Human Reproduction Poster

Have pupils organise key information into a clear poster and explain it verbally, using age-appropriate scientific language.

📡 Nervous System Signalling

Use a simple signal-passing activity to model how information is transmitted between the central nervous system and the body.

🕵️ Microorganism Detective

Sort examples and describe the types of microorganisms. Follow school safety guidance for any investigation.

🌱 Plant Competition Investigation

Guide pupils to observe how plants compete for resources and record findings in a table or labelled drawing.

🦋 Conservation Exhibition

Make a visual exhibition about threatened species, causes of threats and practical conservation actions.

🎯 Assessment Guide

Use the Performance Standards in the sheet as the reference when choosing the expected pupil evidence. Evidence can include identifying, describing, explaining, predicting, investigating, organising findings and communicating creatively, depending on the learning standard.

Teacher note: The uploaded reference sheet contains some wording and alignment irregularities. Check the original document before using any row as an official assessment descriptor.

⚡ Quick Check

Try these short revision questions.

1. Which system includes the brain and spinal cord?
2. Which is an example of a plant resource that may be competed for?
3. Why do we conserve threatened species?
